cards.headline: Does Your Korean Registration Cover an Imported Serum?
body: Your factory can make it. What must be ready before you import and sell it?
cards.takeaway: A domestic OEM registration alone does not complete the import-and-sale process.
cards.design: Place an overseas shipment opposite a Korean responsible cosmetics distributor registration, with the missing import-document checkpoint between them.

cards.headline: Domestic OEM or Import? Check Your Registration

body.text: Covers products made under contract by a registered Korean cosmetics manufacturer, not products imported directly.
Covers imported cosmetics sold in Korea; if it is already registered, do not add the same type again.

cards.takeaway: If type (c) is missing, file the change within 30 days and before importing.
cards.design: Magnify the business-type field on the Korean registration and contrast Type (b) with Type (c); keep the 30-day condition in a secondary badge.

cards.headline: The Two Certificates Prove Different Things

body.text: The Certificate of Manufacture identifies the maker, product, ingredients, relevant quantities, specifications, and supporting details.
The Certificate of Sale confirms that the named product is sold in the country of manufacture or sale.

cards.takeaway: Before ordering, confirm who issues each certificate and whether notarization is required.
cards.design: Show two clearly labelled documents: formula and maker details on one, issuing authority and product name on the other.

cards.headline: Korea-Only Serum: No Local Sales Record

body.text: For a product sold locally, identify the Certificate of Sale issuer.
A new serum may have no local sales history under that name.
If issuance is difficult, ask KPTA which documents and procedure apply.

cards.takeaway: Do not order assuming an unverified substitute will be accepted.
cards.design: Contrast a locally sold serum with a Korea-only launch, then show a documented KPTA inquiry instead of an invented substitute certificate.

cards.headline: Match the Same Product Across Four Records
head: Record
Compare

body.text: Importer name, address, and registration number
Actual maker, English product name, and ingredients
Certified English name and batch number
Final quantity, specification, and value

cards.takeaway: Start where the factory's internal code differs from the certified English product name.
cards.design: Use a saveable four-row document-matching worksheet with exact comparison fields and restrained document silhouettes.

cards.headline: Pre-Clearance Is Not Customs Clearance

body.text: Match importer registrations
Code the final ingredient list
File the electronic report
Make a separate import declaration

cards.note: File the report before every import
cards.takeaway: A KPTA report does not replace the separate customs import declaration.
cards.design: Build four compact checkpoints and draw a firm visual boundary between KPTA reporting and the customs declaration.

cards.headline: When Item and Ingredient-List Codes Change

body.text: Changed ingredients or quantities require a new item code and ingredient-list code.
A new 50 mL size with the same formula uses a new item code and the existing ingredient-list code.

cards.takeaway: Reimporting the same unchanged item may reuse its item code.
cards.design: Contrast a changed formula with unchanged 30 mL and 50 mL bottles; visually separate item codes from ingredient-list codes.

cards.headline: After Customs: Check Each Batch and Label

body.text: Keep A001 and A002 quality records separate.
Record imports and tests by batch, and sales by buyer.
Match product, ingredient, batch, and expiry details to the Korean label.

cards.takeaway: A foreign test report alone does not establish a Korean testing exemption.
cards.design: Lead separate A001 and A002 packages to distinct quality records, an import ledger, and a Korean label.

cards.headline: Ready to Manufacture Is Not Ready to Import
body: Before ordering, confirm who issues both certificates and when they will arrive.
cards.takeaway: Place your Korean registration beside the overseas factory's documents before the first order.
cards.design: Use one large central contrast, with an overseas shipment on one side and the Korean registration on the other.

cards.headline: Start With the Documents You Already Have

body.text: Your registration, available certificates or issuance details, product name, and final ingredient information.
We compare the business type, product name, and maker, then identify what else to request.

cards.takeaway: ETHOS Administrative Attorney Office offers a free preliminary document review.
cards.design: Put the importer's existing documents on the left and product-name, manufacturer, and registration mismatches on the right; keep one understated free-review line below.
